newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace says it restructures packaging unit.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace says it restructures packaging unit.

text.p: W. R. Grace & Co. said Wednesday it will reorganize its packaging unit to replace its regional management with a global structure.
Grace's packaging unit produces laminates and shrinkable films and bags to protect food and non-food consumer products under the registered trade names Cryovac, Formpac, Omicron, Cypress and DAREX.

The unit, with 12,000 employees and operations in 100 countries, contributes two-thirds of Grace's $3.5 billion in annual sales. More than half of the packaging unit's sales are derived outside North America, Grace said.
Under the reorganization, the packaging unit's global headquarters will relocate to Duncan, S.C., and its Latin America headquarters will relocate to Mexico City, the company said.

"This move to a truly global organization is expected to accelerate our growth and improve our manufacturing capital productivity, lower costs and shorten product development time," said Albert Costello, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Grace. "By managing this business on a global basis, we should be even more agile and efficient in meeting customer needs, whether they are global or local," he added.

Management appointments include four global functional leaders: Al Weinberg, vice president of global technology; Ken Costanzo, vice president of global marketing and business development; Chris Woodbridge, vice president of global manufacturing; and Phil Ryan, vice president of global finance and information technology.

"These changes, and the continuous operating improvements we expect to result from these changes, are supportive of the financial targets that we've set for our packaging business and Grace," said Costello.
